Q: Recoding in R without typing the original variable values? A:

Another solution with base R:

example_df$id2 <- sapply(example_df$id, FUN=grep, strings)

replaces the id value strings by their index.

Q: Reloading submodules in IPython A:

IPython comes with some automatic reloading magic:

%load_ext autoreload
%autoreload 2

It will reload all changed modules every time before executing a new line. The way this works is slightly different than dreload. Some caveats apply, type %autoreload? to see what can go wrong.

If you want to always enable this settings, modify your IPython configuration file ~/.ipython/profile_default/ipython_config.py[1] and appending:

c.InteractiveShellApp.extensions = ['autoreload']
c.InteractiveShellApp.exec_lines = ['%autoreload 2']

Credit to @Kos via a comment below.

[1] If you don't have the file ~/.ipython/profile_default/ipython_config.py, you need to call ipython profile create first. Or the file may be located at $IPYTHONDIR.

Q: How does one make a player diagram/visualization like the one below within Python? A:

After watching on this page a similar example of that chart (and while browsing as well), I think that you could try the following:

  • Use Photoshop (or any other way) for modify the image of a cropped baseball player and get a similar result as the shown above.
  • Use said modified image as background of your chart.
  • Get familiar with the documentation of the chart API you want to use for this purpose - in order to check how you can modify the styles of the lineplots and other parts of the chart.

I believe that the result you show on your question is made in that way - I do not think that there is any available (even free) chart/diagram - this is a heavily-modified/stylized chart.

Q: View Docker entrypoint output A:

First up, I'd make a slight change to your Dockerfile, which you can see below:

COPY entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/

ENTRYPOINT ["entrypoint.sh"]

By copying entrypoint.sh to /usr/local/bin it's in your path. Given that, you don't need to set the executable bit, and can use a simpler version of the ENTRYPOINT instruction. As a result, the Dockerfile is shorter and more concise.

As for debugging, you're on the right path by not detaching the container, rather letting it run in the foreground as it starts, so that the logs will be printed to the terminal. Without knowing what entrypoint.sh contains, it's hard to know what the problem might be.

However, I suggest using the --build and --force-recreate options, in case you've made changes to your Dockerfile since the last time you built the container. I find these two options really helpful when trying to debug a container.
